UNH.rationale: UNH is a durable franchise with strong cash generation, but the current valuation is severely disconnected from fundamentals. GAAP EPS grew just +0.7% YoY (Q1 2026: $6.90 vs Q1 2025: $6.85), revenue only +2.0% YoY, and operating income actually declined (margin compression from 8.3% to 8.0%). Net margin has collapsed from 5.6% to 2.8% and ROE from 22.8% to 12.3% over the past year. Yet the stock trades at 27.2x diluted PE — nearly 2.3x the 11.9x level of a year ago — with an earnings yield of 3.7% sitting 87bps below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.57%. This multiple expansion is almost entirely price-driven, not earnings-driven: the stock is up +31.9% in the quarter to $382.48 while fundamentals deteriorated. The qual report's forward catalysts (2027 MA rate tailwind of 2.48%, AI investment, guidance raise to >$18.25 adjusted EPS) provide optionality but require significant execution proof and assume no adverse regulatory outcomes from the DOJ antitrust investigation into the Optum-UnitedHealthcare relationship. Berkshire Hathaway's full exit of ~5 million shares (disclosed 2026-05-18) after less than a year signals sophisticated capital found the risk/reward unattractive. The adjusted EPS beat narrative ($7.23 vs consensus) masks flat GAAP earnings and includes the $525M Optum UK divestiture gain. A re-rating toward even the 12-month median PE of ~14x — justified by the flat earnings trajectory — implies substantial downside. The risk-reward is deeply unfavorable: the market is paying peak multiples for demonstrably worse profitability, with unresolved regulatory tail risks and a below-risk-free earnings yield.

Stock price +31.9% in quarter to $382.48 on flat earnings — move is entirely multiple expansion, not earnings-driven
Berkshire Hathaway fully exited ~5M shares (disclosed 2026-05-18) after holding less than a year — sophisticated capital walked away
DOJ antitrust investigation into Optum-UnitedHealthcare relationship and MA billing practices remains unresolved — structural de-rating risk
